question: Which of the following mountain passes forms the 'tri-junction' of India, China and Myanmar?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Diphu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Diphu Pass is located at the tri-junction of India, China, and Myanmar.
 
• It is an important strategic location for the three countries, marking the meeting point of their borders.
 
• The pass lies on the McMahon Line, which is the demarcation line between Tibet and India in the eastern sector of the border.
 
• Diphu Pass has historical significance, as it was a part of the ancient trade routes that connected India with China and Southeast Asia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pensi La**

 
 
• Pensi La is a mountain pass in the Ladakh region of India.
 
• It connects the Zanskar Valley to the Suru Valley in the Union Territory of Ladakh.
 
• The pass is situated at an elevation of about 4,400 meters (14,400 feet) above sea level.
 
• Pensi La is primarily used for travel between these valleys and is not located at any international boundary.
 
 
 
• **Bum La**
 
 
• Bum La Pass is located in the Tawang district of Arunachal Pradesh, India.
 
• It is situated near the Indo-China border and is historically significant for being part of the route taken by the Dalai Lama when he fled from Tibet to India in 1959.
 
• The pass is at an elevation of 4,633 meters (15,200 feet).
 
• Bum La Pass is a crucial point for trade and military activities between India and China.
 
 
 
• **Imis La**
 
 
• Imis La is not widely known or recognized as a significant mountain pass.
 
• It does not hold strategic or historical importance in the context of international borders involving India, China, or Myanmar.
 
• There is limited information available about Imis La.
